label: Is selected in army window
summary: Whether this unit is the one selected in the army window, going by its name and its one use.
details: Vanilla uses it in the outliner (the list of armies at the side of the screen) to pick the text of a row's tooltip: when it is true the text says a click goes to the army's location, otherwise that a click selects the army.

label: Is allied unit
summary: Whether this unit on the map belongs to an ally of the player, going by its name and its use on the map icons.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the ally background of an army's map icon, and together with Army.IsControlledByCompanionAI to show the icon of the army's AI order.

label: Is enemy unit
summary: Whether this unit on the map belongs to an enemy of the player, going by its name and its use on the map icons.
details: Vanilla always checks it together with IsUnitItemHostile: either one switches the army's map icon to the enemy version, and neither keeps the normal version. The game does not say how an enemy differs from a hostile unit.

label: Is hostile unit
summary: Whether this unit on the map counts as hostile to the player, going by its name and its use on the map icons.
details: Vanilla shows the enemy version of the army's map icon when the unit is an enemy or hostile. Inside that icon the enemy background and the at-war marker are shown only when it is not hostile,; what makes a unit hostile is not documented.

label: Is own unit
summary: Whether this unit on the map belongs to the player, going by its name and its use on the map icons.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the own-army background on the map icon, and combines it with IsGathering (troops still gathering) and with IsOnlyHiredTroops for other parts of the icon.

label: Is neutral unit
summary: Whether this unit on the map counts as neutral, going by its name and its use on the map icons.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the neutral background on an army's map icon (next to the own, ally, enemy and hostile ones), and combines it with IsGathering for gathering troops.

label: Pan camera to unit
summary: Going by its name, moves the map camera to this unit.
details: Vanilla calls it on a right click on an army row in the outliner. It returns nothing.

label: Select unit and pan
summary: Going by its name, selects this unit and moves the map camera to it.
details: Vanilla calls it on a left click on an army row in the outliner (a right click only pans, with PanToUnit). It returns nothing.

label: Select unit
summary: Going by its name, selects this unit, without moving the camera.
details: Vanilla never calls it on a unit item. The army window has its own SelectUnit on another type (AttachToArmyWindow.SelectUnit), which is only a hint. It returns nothing.

label: Unit itself
summary: The unit item itself, so it can be passed to another function.
details: Vanilla passes it in the army window to AttachToArmyWindow.SelectUnit and AttachToArmyWindow.IsSelectedUnit, so a row can select its own unit and show whether it is the selected one. The game documents no return type.

label: Should be highlighted
summary: Whether this unit's map icon should be highlighted, going by its name.
details: Vanilla shows a part of the map icon when this is true or when the unit is selected (IsSelected). What causes the highlight is not documented.

label: Should be shown
summary: Going by its name, whether this unit should be shown; the game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla never uses it on a unit item. The same name on the rally point map icon (RallyPointMapIcon.ShouldBeShown) is another type and only a hint.

label: Shows gathering progress
summary: Whether the map icon should show that this unit's troops are still gathering, and how far along they are.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the gathering icon and a progress bar filled from the army's gathering progress (Army.GetGatheringProgress).

label: Shows supply icon
summary: Whether the map icon of this unit should show its supply icon.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the supplies widget next to the army's map icon. When exactly the game shows it is not documented.

label: Shows supply trend
summary: Whether the supply icon of this unit should also show the supply trend arrow, going by its name and use.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the supply trend icon inside the supply widget of the army's map icon. What the trend shows (rising or falling supply) is not documented.

label: Access unit map icon
summary: A function on a unit's map icon that, going by its name, hands back the icon itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Displayed unit
summary: The unit that this map icon currently shows, going by its name and use.
details: Vanilla makes it the context of the icon's contents, so the UnitItem functions inside read from that unit. One map icon can stand for several units (see GetUnitItems).

label: Shown unit count
summary: A whole number: how many units this map icon stands for, going by its name and its use.
details: Vanilla shows it in brackets on the icon when it is 2 or more, and compares it with the size of GetUnitItems to show another part when not all of the units are counted.

label: Map icon tooltip
summary: A text: going by its name, the tooltip of this unit map icon.
details: Vanilla never uses it on this type; GetTooltip on other types (diplomatic items, claims, event options) is only a hint.

label: Units in icon
summary: The list of units this map icon stands for.
details: Vanilla lists them in the icon's tooltip and shows that list only when it holds more than one unit; its size is also compared with GetShownCount. The game documents no return type.

label: Click unit map icon
summary: Going by its name, what happens when the unit map icon is clicked; the game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla never calls it on this type; OnClick on other types is only a hint. It returns nothing.

label: Click army in icon
summary: Going by its name and use, reacts to a click on one army listed in the map icon's tooltip.
details: It takes one argument: vanilla passes the army of the clicked row (Army.Self). What the click does (select, pan) is not documented. It returns nothing.

label: Click army group
summary: Going by its name and use, reacts to a click on an army in the map icon, as part of a group of armies.
details: It takes one argument: vanilla passes an army (Army.Self) from a button in the map icon template. What happens with the group is not documented. It returns nothing.

label: Unit map icon itself
summary: A function on a unit's map icon that, going by its name, hands back the icon itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; Self after other types (such as Character.Self) is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access icon handler
summary: A function on the handler of unit map icons that, going by its name, hands back the handler itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint.

label: Unit map icon
summary: The unit map icon that this handler holds, going by its name and use.
details: Vanilla makes it the context of the unit icon parts of the map icon layer, so the UnitMapIcon functions inside read from it. The game documents no return type.

label: Icon handler itself
summary: A function on the handler of unit map icons that, going by its name, hands back the handler itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; Self after other types is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access unit orders
summary: A function on an army's orders that, going by its name, hands back the orders object itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint.

label: Halt order
summary: The order that makes an army stop moving.
details: Vanilla's army window reaches it through an army's orders (`Army.GetOrders.GetHalt`, `ArmyWindow.GetOrders.GetHalt`), checks it with IsValidCommand and sends it with PostCommand when the Halt movement or Halt all Armies button is clicked.

label: Unit orders itself
summary: A function on an army's orders that, going by its name, hands back the orders object itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; Self after other types is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access user data node
summary: A function on a user data node of the engine's internal interface tools that, going by its name, hands back the node itself.
details: The game lists it among its internal GUI functions and vanilla never uses it; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint.

label: Configure node
summary: A function of the engine's internal interface tools on a user data node; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name it configures the node. Vanilla never uses it. It returns nothing.

label: Node ID
summary: A text: going by its name, the ID of a user data node of the engine's internal interface tools.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Node label
summary: A text: going by its name, the label of a user data node of the engine's internal interface tools.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: User data node itself
summary: A function on a user data node of the engine's internal interface tools that, going by its name, hands back the node itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; Self after other types is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Node type name
summary: Going by its name, the name of the type of a user data node of the engine's internal interface tools.
details: Vanilla never uses it, and the game documents no return type.

label: Access value breakdown
summary: A function on a value breakdown (a number shown with the parts it is made of) that, going by its name, hands back the breakdown itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint.

label: Breakdown value as number
summary: The total of this value breakdown as a decimal number that can be calculated with.
details: Vanilla uses it in the tax collector texts to subtract another value from it and show the difference. GetValue is the text version.

label: Breakdown name
summary: The name of this value breakdown, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as "name: value" in breakdown lines, and in the administrative vassal details hides the line when the name is empty.

label: Breakdown parts
summary: The list of parts that make up this value breakdown.
details: Vanilla counts them (GetDataModelSize) in the tax collector windows, for example to show how many vassals or tax jurisdictions are in use out of the maximum. The game documents no return type.

label: Parts, smallest first
summary: Going by its name, the parts of this value breakdown sorted from smallest to largest.
details: Vanilla never uses it; the descending version is used (see GetSubValuesDescending). The game documents no return type.

label: Parts, largest first
summary: The parts of this value breakdown sorted from largest to smallest, going by its name.
details: Vanilla shows the first three of them in the succession event window (DataModelFirst with 3), so the biggest contributions come first.

label: Breakdown value
summary: The total of this value breakdown as ready-made text.
details: Vanilla shows it after the gold or soldier icon for tax contributions, and as the maximum number of tax collectors. GetFixedPointValue is the number version.

label: Value indicator
summary: A text: going by its name, a marker of how high or low this value is, between two limits.
details: It takes two arguments, which vanilla never shows because it never uses this function. Its sibling GetValueIndicatorHideNone is given a low and a high number.

label: Value indicator, hide none
summary: A text marking how high or low this value is between two numbers, which going by its name is left out when there is nothing to show.
details: It takes two arguments: vanilla passes -5 and 1 in the county view, next to the county's development, for governments affected by development. How the marker looks is not documented.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Going by vanilla's use, the low end.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: Going by vanilla's use, the high end.

label: Simple value indicator
summary: A text: going by its name, a simple marker of how high or low this value is.
details: Vanilla never uses it and it takes no arguments, unlike GetValueIndicator.

label: Has tooltip
summary: Whether this value breakdown has a tooltip to show.
details: Vanilla uses it to switch tooltips on in the HUD and, with ShouldShowValue, to choose between a breakdown line with or without a tooltip.

label: Value breakdown itself
summary: A function on a value breakdown that, going by its name, hands back the breakdown itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; Self after other types is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Should show value
summary: Whether the number of this value breakdown should be shown.
details: Vanilla checks it in the shared value breakdown lines and the tax slot vassal window before showing the value, once with a tooltip and once without.

label: Variable value editor
summary: The editor for the value of one variable in the engine's inspector tools.
details: The inspector shows it next to the variable's name box, as a box where the value (an object or a number) can be read and changed.

label: Access variable entry
summary: A function on a variable entry of the engine's internal variable tools that, going by its name, hands back the entry itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint.

label: Delete variable
summary: Deletes this variable in the engine's inspector tools; it returns nothing.
details: The inspector runs it from the X button at the end of the variable's row, with the tooltip "Delete variable".

label: Variable name
summary: The name of this variable in the engine's inspector tools.
details: The inspector shows it in an editable box at the start of the variable's row; SetName saves a changed name.

label: Variable entry itself
summary: A function on a variable entry of the engine's internal variable tools that, going by its name, hands back the entry itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; Self after other types is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Rename variable
summary: Saves the name typed into this variable's name box in the engine's inspector tools; it returns nothing.
details: The inspector runs it when editing of the name box ends. It takes no value: the name comes from the box itself.

label: Access variable info
summary: A function on one variable shown in the debug watch window that, going by its name, hands back that entry itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint.

label: Variable expiry date
summary: The date on which this variable runs out, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it in the debug watch window (a debug tool that shows variables), only when the variable has an expiry date (HasExpirationDate).

label: Variable name
summary: The name of this variable, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it in the list of variables in the debug watch window.

label: Variable value
summary: The value of this variable, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it next to the name in the debug watch window.

label: Has expiry date
summary: Whether this variable runs out on a set date.
details: Vanilla uses it in the debug watch window to show the expiry date (GetExpirationDate) only when there is one.

label: Variable info itself
summary: A function on one variable of the debug watch window that, going by its name, hands back that entry itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; Self after other types is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access inspector entry
summary: A function on an entry of the engine's internal variable inspector that, going by its name, hands back the entry itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint.

label: Inspected variable
summary: The variable that this row of the engine's variable inspector stands for.
details: The inspector shows the variable's name, value and remaining time from it, with a delete button beside them.

label: Delete variable
summary: Deletes the variable of this row in the engine's variable inspector; it returns nothing.
details: The inspector runs it from the X button with the tooltip "Delete variable".

label: Inspector entry itself
summary: A function on an entry of the engine's internal variable inspector that, going by its name, hands back the entry itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; Self after other types is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access variable inspector
summary: A function on the engine's internal variable inspector that, going by its name, hands back the inspector itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint.

label: New variable
summary: The variable being filled in under "Add new variable" in the engine's variable inspector, before it is added.
details: The inspector shows its name, value and remaining time boxes; the + button next to them (AddVariable) adds it.

label: Inspected variables
summary: The list of variables the engine's variable inspector shows.
details: The inspector draws one row per variable from it, under a heading with their count (GetNumVariables). The game documents no return type.

label: Add variable
summary: Adds the variable filled in under "Add new variable" in the engine's variable inspector; it returns nothing.
details: The inspector runs it from the + button next to the new variable's boxes (AccessSetupVariable).

label: Number of variables
summary: How many variables the engine's variable inspector lists, as a whole number.
details: The inspector shows it in the heading "Variables (… entries)".

label: Variable inspector itself
summary: A function on the engine's internal variable inspector that, going by its name, hands back the inspector itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; Self after other types is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Variable value editor
summary: The editor for the value of a variable in the engine's variable inspector.
details: The inspector shows it between the variable's name box and its remaining time box, as a box where the value (an object or a number) can be read and changed.

label: Access inspector variable
summary: A function on a variable of the engine's internal variable inspector that, going by its name, hands back the variable entry itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint.

label: Variable name
summary: The name of a variable in the engine's variable inspector.
details: The inspector shows it in an editable box with the tooltip "Variable name"; SetName saves a changed name.

label: Time until deleted
summary: How many ticks (steps of game time) are left before a variable in the engine's variable inspector is deleted, as a whole number.
details: The inspector shows it in an editable box with the tooltip "Ticks until deleted"; SetRemainingTicks saves a changed number.

label: Inspector variable itself
summary: A function on a variable of the engine's internal variable inspector that, going by its name, hands back the variable entry itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; Self after other types is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Rename variable
summary: Saves the name typed into a variable's name box in the engine's variable inspector; it returns nothing.
details: The inspector runs it when editing of the name box ends. It takes no value: the name comes from the box itself.

label: Set time until deleted
summary: Saves the number of ticks typed into a variable's "Ticks until deleted" box in the engine's variable inspector; it returns nothing.
details: The inspector runs it when editing of the box ends. It takes no value: the number comes from the box itself.

label: Variable list entries
summary: The entries of a variable list (a named list of objects kept in a variable) in the engine's inspector tools.
details: The inspector draws one row per entry from it, under the list's name and size. The game documents no return type.

label: Access variable list
summary: A function on a variable list of the engine's internal variable tools that, going by its name, hands back the list itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint.

label: Delete variable list
summary: Going by its name, deletes this variable list in the engine's internal variable tools.
details: Vanilla never calls it on this type; Delete on other types is only a hint. It returns nothing.

label: Variable list name
summary: The name of a variable list in the engine's inspector tools.
details: The inspector shows it as the list's heading, as in "(name) (… entries)".

label: Variable list size
summary: How many entries a variable list holds in the engine's inspector tools, as a whole number.
details: The inspector shows it after the list's name, as in "(name) (… entries)".

label: Variable list itself
summary: A function on a variable list of the engine's internal variable tools that, going by its name, hands back the list itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; Self after other types is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Entry value editor
summary: The editor for the object held by one entry of a variable list in the engine's inspector tools.
details: The inspector shows it at the start of the entry's row, as a box where the object can be read and changed.

label: Access list entry
summary: A function on one entry of a variable list in the engine's internal variable tools that, going by its name, hands back the entry itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint.

label: Delete list entry
summary: Removes this entry from its variable list in the engine's inspector tools; it returns nothing.
details: The inspector runs it from the X button at the end of the entry's row.

label: Time until deleted
summary: How many ticks (steps of game time) are left before this entry of a variable list is deleted, as a whole number.
details: The inspector shows it in an editable box with the tooltip "Ticks until deleted"; SetTicksRemaining saves a changed number.

label: List entry itself
summary: A function on one entry of a variable list in the engine's internal variable tools that, going by its name, hands back the entry itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; Self after other types is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Set time until deleted
summary: Saves the number of ticks typed into a list entry's "Ticks until deleted" box in the engine's inspector tools; it returns nothing.
details: The inspector runs it when editing of the box ends. It takes no value: the number comes from the box itself.

label: Variable list store
summary: The store of variable lists that the engine's variable list inspector shows.
details: The inspector uses it as the data of its whole panel: the lists, their entries and the boxes for adding a new entry.

label: Access list inspector
summary: A function on the engine's internal variable list inspector that, going by its name, hands back the inspector itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint.

label: List inspector itself
summary: A function on the engine's internal variable list inspector that, going by its name, hands back the inspector itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; Self after other types is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: New entry editor
summary: The editor for the object of a new entry about to be added to a variable list in the engine's inspector tools.
details: The inspector shows it under "Add new entry to list:", next to the list name box and the ticks box; the + button (AddNewEntry) adds it.

label: Access list store
summary: A function on a store of variable lists in the engine's internal tools that, going by its name, hands back the store itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint.

label: Variable lists
summary: The variable lists held in this store of the engine's inspector tools.
details: The inspector draws each list from it, with its name, size and entries. The game documents no return type.

label: Add list entry
summary: Adds the new entry filled in under "Add new entry to list:" to the named variable list in the engine's inspector tools; it returns nothing.
details: The inspector runs it from the + button, whose tooltip names the list the entry goes to.

label: Target list name
summary: The name of the variable list a new entry will be added to, as typed in the engine's inspector tools.
details: The inspector shows it in a box with the tooltip "Which list to add the entry to" and in the + button's tooltip; SetNewVariableListName saves a changed name.

label: Number of variable lists
summary: How many variable lists this store of the engine's inspector tools holds, as a whole number.
details: The inspector shows it in the heading "Variable Lists (… entries)"; the script runner shows it as "Scope Lists (… entries)" for its saved scope lists.

label: New entry duration
summary: How many ticks (steps of game time) a new variable list entry will last before it is deleted, as typed in the engine's inspector tools.
details: The inspector shows it in a box with the tooltip "Ticks until deleted" under "Add new entry to list:"; SetVariableTicksRemaining saves a changed number.

label: List store itself
summary: A function on a store of variable lists in the engine's internal tools that, going by its name, hands back the store itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; Self after other types is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Set target list name
summary: Saves the list name typed into the "Which list to add the entry to" box of the engine's inspector tools; it returns nothing.
details: The inspector runs it when editing of the box ends. It takes no value: the name comes from the box itself.

label: Set new entry duration
summary: Saves the number of ticks typed for a new variable list entry in the engine's inspector tools; it returns nothing.
details: The inspector runs it when editing of the "Ticks until deleted" box ends. It takes no value: the number comes from the box itself.

label: New variable editor
summary: The editor for the value of a new variable about to be added in the engine's inspector tools.
details: The inspector shows it under "Add new entry:", next to the name box; the + button (AddNewEntry) adds the variable.

label: Access variable store
summary: A function on a store of variables in the engine's internal tools that, going by its name, hands back the store itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint.

label: Stored variables
summary: The variables held in this store of the engine's inspector tools.
details: The inspector draws one row per variable from it, with its name, value and a delete button. The game documents no return type.

label: Add variable
summary: Adds the new variable filled in under "Add new entry:" to this store of the engine's inspector tools; it returns nothing.
details: The inspector runs it from the + button, whose tooltip names the new variable.

label: New variable name
summary: The name typed for a new variable in the engine's inspector tools.
details: The inspector shows it in a box with the tooltip "The name of the new variable" and in the + button's tooltip; SetNewVariableName saves a changed name.

label: Number of variables
summary: How many variables this store of the engine's inspector tools holds, as a whole number.
details: The inspector shows it in the heading "Variables (… entries)"; the script runner shows it as "Scopes (… entries)" for its saved scopes.

label: Variable store itself
summary: A function on a store of variables in the engine's internal tools that, going by its name, hands back the store itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; Self after other types is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Set new variable name
summary: Saves the name typed for a new variable in the engine's inspector tools; it returns nothing.
details: The inspector runs it when editing of the name box ends. It takes no value: the name comes from the box itself.

label: Access GUI variables
summary: A function on the interface's variable system that, going by its name, hands back the system itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint.

label: Clear GUI variable
summary: Removes a named variable of the interface, so it no longer exists.
details: Vanilla uses these named interface variables to remember things like which tab or popup is open. Vanilla calls it on clicks and when a window opens, for example to close a popup or reset a view. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the interface variable.
fields.values: a text in quotes, such as 'activity_locale_popup'

label: Clear GUI variable if
summary: Removes a named variable of the interface, but only when a condition is true.
details: Vanilla uses it, for example, to close a target list when the chosen intent has no target, or to close the trait selection in the ruler designer when another interface variable exists. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the interface variable.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The condition; the variable is removed only when it is true.
fields.values: a yes/no expression, such as Not( ActivityIntent.HasTarget )

label: GUI variable exists
summary: Whether a named variable of the interface currently exists.
details: Vanilla uses it very often to show or hide parts of windows, for example a list that appears while its variable is set. Use HasValue to check for a particular value.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the interface variable.

label: GUI variable value
summary: The current value of a named variable of the interface, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as text (for example a doctrine group name in the faith creation window) and reads it to set another variable.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the interface variable.

label: GUI variable has value
summary: Whether a named variable of the interface is set to a given value.
details: Vanilla uses it to show which tab is active and to show only that tab's contents, paired with Set on the tab buttons.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the interface variable.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.values: a text in quotes, such as 'history'

label: GUI variables itself
summary: A function on the interface's variable system that, going by its name, hands back the system itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; Self after other types is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Set GUI variable
summary: Sets a named variable of the interface to a value.
details: Vanilla uses it on tab buttons and similar clicks, for example to switch the artifact details to the history tab. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the interface variable.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.values: a text in quotes, or a text expression

label: Set or toggle GUI variable
summary: Sets a named variable of the interface to a value or, going by its name, clears it when it already has that value.
details: Vanilla uses it on tab buttons in the royal court and on a switch in the coat of arms designer, so a second click undoes the first. The exact toggle rule is not documented. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the interface variable.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.values: a text in quotes, such as 'artifacts'

label: Toggle GUI variable
summary: Switches a named variable of the interface on or off: creates it when missing and, going by its name, removes it when it exists.
details: Vanilla uses it on buttons that open and close parts of the interaction window. The game gives it a yes/no return value; what that value means is not documented.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the interface variable.

label: Access vassal conversion
summary: A function on the vassal conversion part of the faith and culture creation windows that, going by its name, hands back that part itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint.

label: Conversion actor
summary: The character whose vassal or subordinate the character in a given row of the conversion list is.
details: It takes one argument: vanilla passes the row number (CharacterListItem.GetIndex) and shows the returned character's titled first name, as in "vassal of ..." or "subordinate of ...". The game documents no return type.

label: Number of subordinates
summary: A whole number: how many subordinates are listed for conversion when a new faith is created.
details: Vanilla shows it as the total in "X of Y subordinates will convert" and shows the conversion list when this or GetNumberOfVassals is above 0. Which characters count as subordinates rather than vassals is not documented.

label: Subordinates to convert
summary: A whole number: how many of the listed subordinates will convert to the new faith.
details: Vanilla shows it as the first number in "X of Y subordinates will convert" in the faith creation window.

label: Number of vassals
summary: A whole number: how many vassals are listed for conversion when a new faith or culture is created.
details: Vanilla shows it as the total in "X of Y vassals will convert" in the faith creation and culture hybridization windows.

label: Vassals to convert
summary: A whole number: how many of the listed vassals will convert to the new faith or culture.
details: Vanilla shows it as the first number in "X of Y vassals will convert".

label: Vassal conversion list
summary: The list of vassals shown for conversion in the faith creation window, going by its name and use.
details: Vanilla makes it the context of the list part of the window. The game documents no return type.

label: Is subordinate
summary: Whether the character in a given row of the conversion list is a subordinate rather than a vassal.
details: It takes one argument: vanilla passes the row number (CharacterListItem.GetIndex) and picks the text "subordinate of" or "vassal of" with it.

label: Vassal conversion itself
summary: A function on the vassal conversion part of the faith and culture creation windows that, going by its name, hands back that part itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; Self after other types is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access vassal stance
summary: A function on a vassal stance (a group of vassals that the My Realm window counts and shows an opinion for) that, going by its name, hands back the stance itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint.

label: Stance description
summary: The description text of this vassal stance.
details: Vanilla shows it in the stance's tooltip.

label: Stance icon
summary: The icon picture of this vassal stance.
details: Vanilla uses it as the texture of an icon in vassal lists and the tax slot vassal window. The game documents no return type.

label: Stance opinion sources
summary: A text listing where the opinion of vassals with this stance towards a given character comes from.
details: It takes one argument: vanilla passes the character of the My Realm window and shows the result under "Sources" in the stance's tooltip, after the opinion value from GetModifierValueFor.

label: Stance opinion
summary: The opinion that vassals with this stance have of a given character, as a number.
details: It takes one argument: vanilla passes the character of the My Realm window, shows the value in the stance's tooltip and colours it by how good or bad the opinion is.

label: Stance name
summary: The name of this vassal stance.
details: Vanilla shows it after the stance icon in the My Realm window's stance tooltip. GetNameNoTooltip gives the name without its own tooltip.

label: Stance name, no tooltip
summary: The name of this vassal stance, without the tooltip link that GetName carries, going by its name.
details: Vanilla uses it inside a tooltip, after the plain stance icon (GetTextIconNoFormat), inside a tooltip.

label: Stance preferred heir
summary: Going by its name, the heir that vassals with this stance would prefer, for a given input; the game documents nothing more.
details: It takes one argument, which vanilla never shows because it never uses this function. The game documents no return type.

label: Stance text icon
summary: The icon of this vassal stance for use inside a text.
details: Vanilla puts it before the stance name in the My Realm window's stance tooltip. The game documents no return type.

label: Plain stance text icon
summary: The icon of this vassal stance for use inside a text, going by its name without extra formatting.
details: Vanilla uses it next to vassal counts in the My Realm window and in the stance filter entries. How it differs from GetTextIcon is not documented.

label: Has stance icon
summary: Going by its name, whether this vassal stance has an icon.
details: Vanilla never uses it on this type; HasIcon on other types (laws, game concepts) is only a hint.

label: Vassal stance itself
summary: The vassal stance itself, so it can be passed to another function.
details: Vanilla passes it to MyRealmWindow.GetNumVassalsWithStance to count the vassals with this stance, and hides the stance's row when that count is 0. The game documents no return type.

label: Access stance filter
summary: A function on a vassal stance filter of the My Realm window that, going by its name, hands back the filter itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint.

label: Filtered stance
summary: The vassal stance this filter entry of the My Realm window stands for.
details: Vanilla shows its icon and name in the filter list and in the tooltip "Show ... vassals".

label: Vassals with stance
summary: A whole number: how many vassals this stance filter would show.
details: Vanilla shows it in brackets after the stance's name in the filter list.

label: Is all filter
summary: Whether this filter entry is the one that shows all vassals instead of one stance.
details: Vanilla picks the text "All" and its tooltip for it, and the stance's name for the other entries.

label: Stance filter itself
summary: A function on a vassal stance filter of the My Realm window that, going by its name, hands back the filter itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; Self after other types is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access viewer entity
summary: A function on a viewer entity of the engine's internal tools that, going by its name, hands back the entity itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is another type and only a hint.

label: Current frame
summary: A whole number: going by its name, the frame an entity shown in the engine's internal viewer is at.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Current time
summary: A decimal number: going by its name, the time an entity shown in the engine's internal viewer is at.
details: Vanilla never uses it.
